rows: Penny to ping-pong ball size hail fell on U.S. Highway 87 east-southeast of Lees.
Quarter to half-dollar size hail fell in Garden City.
A NWS cooperative observer reported many limbs broken off trees at her property as well as some tin that was blown off her barn roof.
The public reported that winds had damaged windmills, irrigation pivots, and had blown a tractor over north of Garden City.
Soft marble to penny size hail fell in Lees.

A spotter north of Garden City reported that a storage shed was knocked down and a golf cart was tipped over by thunderstorm winds.
Sixty mph winds were reported in St. Lawrence. No damage was reported.
A 62 mph wind gust was reported from the Reagon and Glasscock County line. No damage was reported.

Strong thunderstorm winds down several trees in Garden City.
A fence was blown down and power was lost in Garden City.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 60 mph wind gust in Garden City.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced golfball sized hail near Garden City. This hail caused significant car damage. The cost of damage is a rough estimate.
Law enforcement reported that 10 power poles had been snapped near Lees by winds produced from thunderstorms in Glasscock County. The wind speed and cost of damage are a rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 60 mph wind gust north of Garden City. No damage was reported.
A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 60 mph wind gust northeast of Garden City.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 62 mph wind gust near St. Lawrence as recorded by the local mesonet site.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 66 mph wind gust four miles southwest of St. Lawrence.
A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 65 mph wind gust nine miles southwest of Garden City.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced wind damage northwest of Garden City along Farm to Market Road 415. Power poles were blown down along this road. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced wind damage in the northeast part of the county. Five power poles were blown down along Highway 87. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.
A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced a 64 mph wind gust four miles southwest of St. Lawrence.
A thunderstorm produced a landspout tornado seven miles north of St. Lawrence. The landspout remained over open field and no damage was reported.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced wind damage 13 miles west of Garden City. Several power poles were blown down along State Highway 158 at State Highway 137. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced wind damage in St. Lawrence. Doors were ripped off of a metal barn. The wind speed was estimated at 65 to 70 mph. The time was estimated by radar. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm moved across Glasscock County and produced wind damage twelve miles north of Garden City. A roof was blown off, a porch was destroyed, and a fence was blown down. The cost of damage is a very rough estimate.

A thunderstorm produced a 58 mph wind gust at the Mesonet site near Saint Lawrence.
A fence was reported blown down with an RV shifted due to strong winds. Wind speeds were estimated to be 80 mph. Property damage cost is an estimation.
Ping pong ball-sized hail reported by NWS employee about 5 miles ENE of Saint Lawrence. Time is estimated from radar.
